title: Matter & Mixtures
description: Grade 5 Science: matter and mixtures — states of matter, what a mixture is, solutions, separating mixtures by sieving, filtering, magnets and evaporation, and clean water.

topics.title: States of Matter Revisited
topics.concept:
All matter is made of tiny particles. The state of matter depends on how those particles are arranged:

  • 🧊 Solid — particles packed tight and barely move; keeps its shape.
  • 💧 Liquid — particles a little looser and can slide; flows and takes the container's shape.
  • 💨 Gas — particles far apart and move fast; spreads to fill all space.

Adding heat makes particles move more, which can melt a solid or boil a liquid.

recap: Matter is made of tiny particles.
Solid: packed tight; liquid: looser; gas: far apart.
Heat makes particles move more and can change the state.

wonder.text: We met solids, liquids and gases before. But what is really happening to the tiny particles inside when matter changes state?

qa.q: What happens to particles when ice melts?
qa.a: Heat gives the packed ice particles more energy, so they start to slide past each other. The solid becomes a liquid — that is melting!

qa.q: Why can we squeeze a gas but not a solid?
qa.a: A gas has lots of empty space between its particles, so they can be pushed closer together. A solid's particles are already packed tight, with no room to squeeze.

topics.title: What Is a Mixture?
topics.concept:
A mixture is made when two or more things are mixed together but are NOT joined to become something new. Each thing keeps its own properties.

  • 🥗 A fruit salad — different fruits mixed together.
  • 🌾 Rice with small stones in it.
  • 🏖️ Sand mixed with iron bits.
  • 🥤 Sugar stirred into water.

Because the things are not joined, we can usually separate a mixture back into its parts.

recap: A mixture is two or more things mixed but not joined.
Each part keeps its own properties.
Mixtures can usually be separated back into their parts.

wonder.text: A bowl of fruit salad has many fruits, all mixed but still separate. Is that a mixture?

qa.a: Yes! Air is a mixture of several gases — mostly nitrogen and oxygen, plus a little carbon dioxide and water vapour. They are mixed but not joined.

qa.q: How is a mixture different from cooking?
qa.a: In a mixture, things stay themselves and can be separated. When we cook (like baking a cake), a NEW thing is made that cannot be separated back — that is a change, not a mixture.

topics.title: Solutions: Dissolving
topics.concept:
When a solid dissolves completely in a liquid, it makes a special clear mixture called a solution.

  • 🍚 Sugar or salt dissolves in water → a solution. The solid is still there, broken into pieces too tiny to see.
  • 🏖️ Sand does NOT dissolve — it stays separate and sinks.
  • 🔥 Things dissolve faster in warm water and when we stir.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 240 180" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="240" height="180" fill="#eef9ff"/><path d="M78 50 h84 l-10 96 a8 8 0 0 1 -8 7 h-48 a8 8 0 0 1 -8 -7 Z" fill="#cfeeff" stroke="#5aa0e0" stroke-width="2"/><g fill="#ffffff" opacity="0.9"><circle cx="100" cy="80" r="4"/><circle cx="130" cy="95" r="4"/><circle cx="112" cy="110" r="4"/><circle cx="135" cy="125" r="3"/><circle cx="98" cy="125" r="3"/></g><rect x="150" y="20" width="14" height="40" rx="3" fill="#caa23a"/><text x="120" y="175" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#1f7fe0" text-anchor="middle">Sugar dissolves → a solution</text></svg>
recap: A solution forms when a solid dissolves fully in a liquid.
Sugar and salt dissolve; sand does not.
Warm water and stirring help things dissolve faster.

wonder.text: Stir sugar into water and it vanishes. Where does it go?

qa.a: No — it is still in the water as tiny invisible pieces (the water tastes sweet). If the water evaporates away, the sugar is left behind!

qa.q: What is the dissolved thing and the liquid called?
qa.a: The solid that dissolves (like sugar) is the solute, and the liquid that dissolves it (like water) is the solvent. Together they make a solution.

topics.title: Separating Mixtures
topics.concept:
We choose a separating method based on what is in the mixture:

  • ✋ Hand-picking — for big bits, like stones in rice.
  • 🪤 Sieving — shaking through a sieve, like flour from bran.
  • ☕ Filtering — passing through a filter, like mud from water.
  • 🧲 Using a magnet — to pull out iron bits.
  • ☀️ Evaporation — boiling or drying off the water to leave the solid, like salt from sea water.

recap: We pick the method to suit the mixture.
Hand-pick, sieve, filter, use a magnet, or evaporate.
Salt is taken from sea water by evaporation.

wonder.text: Mum picks stones out of rice, and we filter tea. How do we un-mix a mixture?

qa.q: How do we get salt from sea water?
qa.a: By evaporation! Sea water is left in shallow pans in the Sun. The water slowly evaporates into the air, leaving the salt behind as white crystals.

qa.q: Why use a magnet to separate?
qa.a: A magnet attracts iron and steel. So if a mixture has iron bits (like iron filings in sand), a magnet can pull them out while leaving the sand behind.

topics.title: Pure and Impure Water
topics.concept:
Water often has things mixed in it — mud, germs or salt. Dirty water can make us ill, so we clean it before drinking.

  • ⏳ Letting it settle — mud sinks to the bottom.
  • ☕ Filtering — removes the dirt.
  • 🔥 Boiling — kills tiny germs.
  • 💧 Cleaning machines and water filters make water safe at home.

Clean, safe drinking water is precious — we must never waste it.

recap: Water often has mud, germs or salt mixed in.
We clean it by settling, filtering and boiling.
Clean drinking water is precious — do not waste it.

wonder.text: Rain looks clean, but is ALL water safe to drink? How do we make water pure?

qa.q: Why must we boil water sometimes?
qa.a: Boiling water kills tiny germs we cannot see that can make us ill. After boiling and cooling, the water is safer to drink.
No — sea water is too salty and would make us more thirsty and ill. The salt must be removed first, which is hard and costly, so we drink fresh water instead.

questions.q: In a solid, the tiny particles are…
options: Joined to make a new thing
questions.explanation: In a solid, particles are packed tightly and barely move.

options: Two or more things mixed but not joined
questions.explanation: A mixture is things mixed together but not joined; they keep their own properties.

questions.q: Sugar dissolved fully in water makes a…
questions.explanation: A solid dissolved fully in a liquid makes a solution.

questions.q: Which method pulls out iron bits?
questions.explanation: A magnet attracts and pulls out iron pieces.

questions.q: We get salt from sea water by…
questions.explanation: Evaporating the water leaves the salt behind.
Boiling kills germs and makes water safer to drink.

questions.q: Why can a gas be squeezed but not a solid?
options: A gas has empty space between particles; a solid does not
questions.explanation: A gas has space between particles to squeeze; a solid's particles are already packed.

options: Yes, a mixture of gases like nitrogen and oxygen
Yes, a mixture of water and rock
questions.explanation: Air is a mixture of several gases, mostly nitrogen and oxygen.

questions.q: If salt water evaporates, the salt…
questions.explanation: The water evaporates and the salt is left behind as crystals.

questions.q: Which is the BEST way to remove mud from water?
questions.explanation: Filtering passes the water through and traps the mud.

questions.q: How is making a mixture different from baking a cake?
options: A mixture can be separated; baking makes a new thing that cannot
questions.explanation: A mixture's parts can be separated; baking makes a new substance that cannot be un-made.
